item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00124","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C25","C05","C09"],"selected_candidate_label":"C25","confidence":0.99,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C25 is explicitly identified by the child as the earlier June 3 maritime Board of Inquiry directive and supplies both its distinctive industry-specific language and its complete operative machinery. The child adapts C25 from the previously covered maritime disputes to additional North Atlantic employers and employees while retaining the same threat finding, statutory powers, reporting requirement, and continued-existence provision. C05 and C09 are close examples of the same Board-of-Inquiry form, but C25 is materially stronger because it concerns the same maritime industry and is expressly cross-referenced by the child.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"certain labor disputes (other than those referred to in [DIRECTIVE_REFERENCE] of June 3, 1948, entitled \"Creating a Board of Inquiry to Report on Certain Labor Disputes Affecting the Maritime Industry of the United States\")","parent_excerpt":"there exist certain labor disputes ... between ship owners or operators ... and certain of their employees","explanation":"The child expressly distinguishes its new maritime disputes from those governed by C25, identifying C25 as its antecedent."},{"child_excerpt":"such disputes threaten to result in strikes or lockouts affecting a substantial part of the maritime industry, an industry engaged in trade, commerce, transportation, transmission or communication among the several States and with foreign nations","parent_excerpt":"such disputes threaten to result in strikes or lockouts affecting a substantial part of the maritime industry, an industry engaged in trade, commerce, transportation, transmission, or communication among the several States and with foreign nations","explanation":"This is nearly verbatim, distinctive maritime-industry language rather than merely a shared broad labor topic."},{"child_excerpt":"The Board shall have powers and duties as set forth in Title II of the said Act. The Board shall report to the President in accordance with the provisions of section 206 of the said Act on or before august 20, 1948. Upon the submission of its report, the Board shall continue in existence to perform such other functions as may be required under the said Act, until the Board is terminated by the President.","parent_excerpt":"The Board shall have powers and duties as set forth in Title II of the said Act. The Board shall report to the President in accordance with the provisions of section 206 of the said Act on or before June 11, 1948. Upon the submission of its report, the Board shall continue in existence to perform such other functions as may be required under the said Act, until the Board is terminated by the President.","explanation":"The operative sequence and wording are reproduced almost exactly, with only the report deadline changed."}]}
